original_card.question: Can one precisely specified helper-mixing word satisfy a replacement for the inherited H2/K interface?
methods: Derive a replacement interface lemma and price its implementation.
Seek an exact dirty-input or chronological-cut counterexample to the proposed replacement.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A full boundary contract and paid profile; unchanged scalar counts alone are insufficient.

first_step.inspect: Compare the two false H2/K flags with the unchanged paid profile in its README.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write one replacement H2/K implication for a single helper-star operation, then try to falsify it on dirty inputs.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A legitimate replacement could admit a cheaper bit circuit; scalar savings alone do not alter the selected moment.
allowed_variations: Choose one helper-star or quartet instance; narrow to one boundary implication.
scope_change_triggers: Changing only source count or scalar addition count without an interface argument.

actual_scope: One boundary implication of the inherited H2/K interface, tested exactly: can a common-frame helper entrance (#1253's 366 classes, all 4,954 supports, plus source donors) be compensated after the scatter instead of by a frame-0 prefix? Census on the selected PR589 word and the four merged star words (PR1062/1122/1188/1208), in a sound necessary class (LC-fav), a corrected strict class (A6) and A6 with storage relays (A6R).
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a replacement H2/K interface and a falsification on dirty inputs or chronological cuts. Rather than proposing a new contract, this tests the late-compensation relaxation of the zero-start rule that #1128 (PROOF section 4) and #1179 leave open by name, on fixed A and scatter, one entrance at a time.
bottleneck_link: Scoped negative result on the nonbinding bit side; no kappa. It shows that moving the zero-start helper rule's compensation after the scatter buys no new entrance except one open triple, and gives the reason: after the scatter each target's dirt-only reachable space has dimension at most 5. A positive entrance would only save the pivot's first climb (-H1), which width-8 hosting cancels (#1179, #1253).
stop_rule: Stop once every support of #1253's closure and every source donor is decided in LC-fav and A6 on all five words by two engines, the only LC-fav survivor is classified under A6R, and controls confirm both directions; do not build a witness for an A6R-only survivor beyond reporting it as an open handoff.
evidence: RESULT.json (identical on all five words): 4,954 supports. LC-fav admits only the #1179 kernel pair 444+470 (T empty) and the triple 444+470+578 (T = 8 targets); no single helper, no new pair, 0 of 5,212 source donors. A6 admits only the kernel pair. Relaxation: one nonzero class (the label line of frame 79) with kernel {444+470, 578} in LC-fav and {444+470} in A6. dim W_t <= 5 (LC-fav), <= 4 (A6); covered K incidences 98 and 47 of 18,085. Triple: A6 covers 150 and 197; A6R(T only) 150, 153, 192, 197; A6R all 8, so it is OPEN. Engine 2 agrees on K, the closure (= #1253's certificate) and every space and verdict. Controls: pre-A window admits 4,954/4,954; synthetic word admits 444+470 late at target 150 and its built witness replays (wlib), a negative fails at register 150; K-bit flip, cleared K column and a relaxed carrier frame flip verdicts. 20 tests pass.
author: Sagar Thakrar (thakrarsagar)
ai_assistance: Substantial: Claude (Anthropic) via Claude Code. Parallel read-only scout and judge subagents selected the question (both judges ranked it first); reader subagents and a synthesizer audited the scout's criterion (finding the triple the scout missed and the carrier gap in its strict class) and specified the classes; both engines, the proof note and the controls were then written fresh.

open_questions.question: Can the triple 444+470+578 be realised as a late-compensated entrance with storage relays?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the only support that survives the sound LC-fav test; A6R covers all 8 of its targets only through relays outside T that must later cancel their x77 content.
open_questions.first_step: Instrument census.a6r_coverable to record which relay reads cover each of the 8 targets, build a candidate word from those reads, and test it with wlib.replay and the #1179 literal stream checks.
open_questions.blocked_by: Restoring the relay targets' x77 content, which A6R ignores.

open_questions.question: Do two or more simultaneous entrances admit late compensation where single ones do not?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This census is one entrance at a time; the joint test needs (K_t c_i)_i in {(u c_i)_i : u in W_t} for every t.
open_questions.first_step: Run the joint test over pairs of disjoint supports in the same class V using the W_t spaces in RESULT.json.

open_questions.question: Does a changed scatter (or COPY placement) enlarge the dirt-only spaces enough to admit a late single entrance?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Both A and the scatter are fixed here; the dim W_t <= 5 bound is a property of this scatter.
open_questions.first_step: Recompute W_t with snapshot terms added to scatter rows, which the class already allows, then with one retained total moved.
open_questions.blocked_by: A new COPY changes the paid copy charge; price it with the #1128 section 5 argument first.
